h: Standing Firm in Holiness Through the Year’s Changing Paths

p: In Midrash Tanchuma (on this parshah) (Tanchuma, Nitzavim 1):
why did Moshe make them into a monument?
Because they were passing from one mind to another,
from the mind of Moshe to the mind of Yehoshua," etc.;
"and Yehoshua too made them into a monument," etc.;
every judge and leader of the generation
has a particular way and order
in his course and his conduct in holiness.
הַנְהָגַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וַהֲלִיכָתוֹ
the conduct and course of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
was above the order of this world,
in all the matters and conduct of man;
as in the eating of the mann,
and all their occupation was only in Torah;
And after this they went out from the mind of Moshe
through the holiness of the Land,
and to engage in working the land,
And because of this they needed
to be made into a monument,
so that they would stand firm in their minds,
rather, that they remain in their place,
from the conduct they had had before.
the holiness of the second conduct.
that this parshah is always read
on the last Shabbos of the year,
"And it shall be, from new moon to new moon
"the olah of each Shabbos on its Shabbos":
that on every Shabbos of the whole year
there is a particular renewal of holiness
there is a particular conduct in holiness,
כַּיָּדוּעַ מֵהַשְּׁנֵים עָשָׂר צֵרוּפֵי הֲוָיָ״ה בָּרוּךְ הוּא
as is known from the twelve permutations of the Name Havayah, blessed be He,
that in each month there is a different permutation.
Therefore at the end of the year,
for the renewal of the year,
in all the times of holiness
that passed in the previous year,
in the form of a new conduct
in all the details of the times and occupation of holiness,
there is need for this as well:
to be standing firm and steady,
so that there remains in his hand an enduring hold in the soul
from the holiness of the times
and through this strength he will enter
the level of the holiness of the times
in the renewal of the new year

p: וְאִיתָא עוֹד בִּפְתִיחַת מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ)
And it is further stated at the opening of Midrash Tanchuma (on this parshah):
'The wicked are overturned and are no more,
but the house of the righteous will stand.'
כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִסְתַּכֵּל
As long as HaKadosh Baruch Hu looks
at the deeds of the wicked
"for though I fell, I have risen" (Michah 7:8).
since there is not found within them, inwardly,
they fall and are thrust down
Not so with the holiness of Yisrael,
for in the inwardness of their root
they are attached to Him, may He be blessed;
and as a result, through this,
in all the falls and descents in the world,
they remain enduring in their holiness,
"For seven times the tzaddik falls and rises."
are included the falls, chas v'shalom,
found in the collective souls of Yisrael,
as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said:
And precisely through the fall and descent
the endurance and the standing are built,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת ד, ב)
as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expounded (Berachos 4b):
"She has fallen; she will no more
Because Yisrael are children of the Omnipresent,
are causes of closeness and holiness,
as a man chastises his son
to bring him back to the good.
And this is why these two sidros are read
at the end of the year:
the rebuke in Parshas Ki Savo,
וְהוּא עַל רֶמֶז הַפָּסוּק (תְּהִלִּים כג, ד)
And this is by allusion to the pasuk (Tehillim 23:4):
that a person's heart should not fall within him
that passed over him in the past year.
For they are for the sake of his good,
he will remain enduring in the point of his holiness,
"You are standing today, all of you," etc.,
"from your woodchopper up to your water-drawer";
"for you to pass into the covenant of Hashem your God."
